key_insight: Prompts can overpower the visual input in large vision-language models (LVLMs), inducing “prompt-induced hallucinations”; HalluScope is a benchmark that quantifies and isolates these failures, showing that language-side prompting often drives errors even when vision backbones are strong.
problem_solved: Identifies, measures, and attributes hallucinations caused by prompts in LVLMs, resolving ambiguity about whether failures stem from the vision encoder or from language/prompt effects and providing a standardized way to evaluate prompt-induced errors.
method: Design HalluScope: a controlled benchmark of images paired with systematically varied prompt templates and ground-truth visual queries to elicit and measure hallucinations.
Evaluate a suite of LVLMs across different vision backbones and LLM components, using quantitative hallucination metrics and qualitative labels to attribute error sources.
Run ablations (prompt strength, misinformation prompts, visual occlusion) to disentangle the influence of prompts vs. vision and produce actionable mitigation guidelines.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical diagnostic tool and evidence-based guidance to detect, attribute, and reduce prompt-induced hallucinations, improving model selection, prompt design, and safe deployment of LVLMs.

paper_title: When Prompts Override Vision: Prompt-Induced Hallucinations in LVLMs
paper_authors: Pegah Khayatan, Jayneel Parekh, Arnaud Dapogny, Mustafa Shukor, Alasdair Newson
